title: Russian troops withdraw from Lyman in Donetsk Oblast after Ukrainian encirclement
body:
On 1 October 2022, Russian forces withdrew from Lyman, a city in Ukraine's Donetsk Oblast, after Ukrainian forces encircled it. Russia's Defense Ministry said its outnumbered troops had moved to more favourable positions. Ukraine's air force said it had moved into Lyman, and President Volodymyr Zelensky's chief of staff posted photos of a Ukrainian flag on the town's outskirts.

Lyman was a key link in Russia's front line for ground communications and logistics, about 160 kilometres south-east of Kharkiv. The Associated Press reported that its loss undercut Russia's claims one day after Moscow declared that it had annexed four Ukrainian regions, including Donetsk. Ukrainian officials had said that thousands of Russian troops were at risk of being cut off, a figure that was not independently verified.

Chechnya's leader Ramzan Kadyrov blamed the retreat, without presenting evidence, on a general whom he said was being covered up for by General Staff leaders, and called for more drastic measures. Zelensky vowed to keep fighting to liberate the annexed and other occupied regions. NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg called the annexation the largest attempted seizure of European territory by force since the Second World War.
